subject: Next steps: prompt contribution & eval plan for Papertrail integration
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Kim <alicia.kim@papertrail.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up & request: sample prompts and edge-case inventory

Alicia — thanks again for a solid discovery call this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and the asks we discussed so we can get started on model fit/evals: 

- Goal: Replace your current retrieval-first QA flow for support triage with a lightweight generative assistant that surfaces probable answers + confidence signals for human reviewers.
- Primary concerns: PII leakage (especially customer IDs and full names in support transcripts), model hallucination on internal KB, and throughput during peak hours (5x baseline).
- Data scope: anonymized chat transcripts, KB entries, and a set of canned templates. No full customer PDFs for now.

Action items we agreed on: 
1) Papertrail to share a small prompt set (50–200 examples) covering: typical queries, edge-case queries, safety-sensitive prompts, and a handful of golden responses. CSV format is easiest (columns: id, prompt, context, expected, redaction_flag).
2) If possible, flag any rows that contain PII and call out preferred redaction behavior (mask vs remove).
3) We’ll run a quick canary evaluation on Redwood Dedicated using two candidate model profiles and share a short benchmark report and failure-mode examples.

I attached a short redaction-checklist and an example CSV template to this note to make it easy. Can you get an initial dump by next Wed (7/7)? If you prefer, your engineering team can drop the file in the Drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmark

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben on model recommendations once we have the samples.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
--
redwood.ai

From: Alicia Kim <alicia.kim@papertrail.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: engineering-team@papertrail.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & request: sample prompts and edge-case inventory

Connor — appreciate the clear recap. Team is aligned; we can share a first pass. A few notes from engineering: 

- We can provide ~120 rows by next Wed. We'll scrub obvious PII (emails, full SSNs) but we want your guidance on masking patterns for customer IDs (they look like CT-12345).
- We cannot share verbatim logs that include customer names tied to account numbers; we can provide masked versions and indicate where masking occurred (redaction_flag column).

Attaching example-prompts.csv (redacted) and a short README. Let me know if the CSV layout works or if you need JSON.

Alicia Kim
Head of Product — Papertrail.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Kim <alicia.kim@papertrail.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Model recommendations & evaluation plan (high level)

Alicia / team — thanks for the prompt sample. Quick recommendations to run the initial eval and what we'll measure: 

Recommended model profiles (canary/dev):
- small-lm-q4-8b (quantized 8B) — baseline for latency-sensitive paths, yields faster token throughput with modest quality drop; target median latency < 120ms token.
- redwood-1.2-13b-opt (fp16 / optimized kernels) — higher-quality candidate for cases where recall and reasoning matter. Expect ~2-3x token cost, better factuality on KB-grounded prompts.

Evaluation plan (what we’ll produce after your CSV upload):
- Automated evaluation: exact-match/ROUGE-ish metrics vs golden responses, and calibration of confidence score.
- Safety checks: PII leakage scanner against your redaction flags + a heuristic that looks for patterns (emails, account IDs, full names).
- Edge-case report: 20 worst-performing prompts with model outputs and suggested prompt rewrites.

Formatting requirements (quick):
- CSV columns: id, prompt, context (optional), expected, redaction_flag (yes/no), sensitivity_notes (optional).
- If redaction_flag = yes, include a brief note describing what was removed.

I'll spin up a dev run on a Dedicated pool and share a short benchmark (latency/cost/accuracy) to the Drive link. Also linking an eval report template: https://redwood.console/reports/eval/pt-2028-06

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Kim <alicia.kim@papertrail.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: engineering-team@papertrail.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model recommendations & evaluation plan (high level)

Thanks Ben — two quick clarifications before we hand data to you: 

1) For PII detection: will Redwood's scanner operate on our side (client-side) or will it be run inside your environment? We need to be comfortable that raw identifiers do not leave our VPC.
2) For the small-lm-q4-8b profile, what quantization artifacts should we watch for in completions? Are you recommending temperature changes or prompt-prefixing to avoid confident hallucinations?

From engineering: we prefer the sample CSV to include an extra column called "mask_example" where we show the exact token replacement we used (e.g., CT-#####). Can you confirm that is sufficient for the redaction heuristics?

Alicia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Kim <alicia.kim@papertrail.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & timeline — canary run and responsibilities

Alicia — quick timeline and next steps from our side so you know what to expect: 

- Today: confirm CSV schema including mask_example column (you mentioned) and drop first CSV into Drive.
- Within 48 hours of receiving: we will run a canary eval on a Dedicated dev pool (small-lm-q4-8b + redwood-1.2-13b-opt) and post a short benchmark to the folder.
- By EOW (7/6): we’ll share the edge-case report (20 examples), a short writeup on redaction findings, and suggested prompt rewrites you can adopt.

On your PII concern — we support two options: 
1) Bring-your-own-key + Private deployment path (we run evals in your VPC so raw identifiers never leave your network).
2) If you prefer Hosted evals, we will run the scanner server-side but only on redacted data; we can provide a signed DPA addendum and a short SOC excerpt for the evaluation window.

If you confirm the CSV layout and preferred run option (1 or 2), we’ll queue the canary. Also attaching a brief action plan (papertrail-eval-plan.docx) that maps responsibilities.

Thanks — excited to get started.
Marissa Cole
Lead, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
